name: 17973-imagechat-qwen25vl3b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
architecture: Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration, bf16, 3.75B params: a 32-layer windowed ViT over a 36-layer decoder (hidden 2048, 16 query heads, 2 KV heads). Shapes are in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: constant (open loop), rate=50 req/s, warmup 30%. The rate is deliberately above capacity, so arrivals are never the binding constraint.
workload: single-turn image+text chat, 1000 requests, each one 512x512 JPEG plus synthetic text. Prompt text uniform 250-300 tokens, output uniform 150-250 tokens (exact: the backend sets max_tokens with ignore_eos). In guidellm this is `synthetic_text` composed with `synthetic_image` (width=512, height=512, images_per_request=1, gradient/jpeg/quality 85/seed 42), driven in process through the `vllm_python` backend rather than over an HTTP chat endpoint. Images are seeded per request, so every request carries byte-different pixels.
purpose: A single-GPU photo question-answering assistant on a 3B multimodal model, handling fifty single-turn image-plus-text requests per second.
launch:
model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct
max-num-seqs: 1024
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
block-size: 16
disable-log-requests: true
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-model-len: 4096
# Inline JSON on ONE line: the launcher reads this file with a flat line reader that drops
# indented block mappings silently. The fast image processor halves the per-request CPU the
# client spends turning one 512x512 JPEG into pixel_values (23.4 ms -> 11.9 ms, measured in
# this arm's venv) and produces the identical 36x36 grid / 324 image tokens.
mm-processor-kwargs: {"use_fast": true}
